name: Javan
overview: Javan is a male figure in the Bible known primarily as the son of Japheth, as recorded in Genesis 10:2. There are no additional tribal affiliations or notable personal attributes mentioned beyond his paternal lineage. His role is primarily genealogical within the biblical record.
namesAndTitles: The name Javan appears as a proper name in Genesis 10:2 without any specific meaning or divine origin provided. It is simply used to identify this biblical individual without further etymological explanation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Javan as the son of Japheth. Additionally, Javan is noted as the father of Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim according to Genesis 10:4. These relationships establish him as a patriarchal figure within the genealogies of the nations descended from Japheth.
scriptureSignificance: Javan's significance lies in his place within the Table of Nations, serving as an ancestor to several peoples descended from Japheth. His mention helps trace the lineage and distribution of peoples following the Flood, underscoring God's providential ordering of nations. Though not a central character in biblical narratives, his genealogical role contributes to the broader understanding of biblical history and God's sovereign plan for humanity.
